verification_questions: Confirm whether the final 2027 Golden Week travel surge affects hotel, transport, and venue demand in Kyoto across April 29-May 5, 2027 (the Cabinet Office holiday list confirms the four national holidays; the actual travel peak varies by year).

evidence.observed_facts: The official Cabinet Office page (www8.cao.go.jp/chosei/shukujitsu/gaiyou.html, fetched 2026-08-13) lists the 2027 national holidays: Showa Day April 29, Constitution Memorial Day May 3, Greenery Day May 4, and Children's Day May 5, with the cluster spanning April 29 through May 5. evidence.inference: Golden Week 2027 creates material hotel and transport demand pressure across Kyoto for that week; recorded as a major logistics awareness flag for Joe, never as an elimination and never as a scheduling decision.

event_name: June rainy season (tsuyu / baiu) in the Kinki region
source_title: Japan Meteorological Agency (official) — Climate of Japan: Baiu rainy season page stating the rainy season lasts from early June to late July across most of Japan
verification_questions: Confirm the 2027 Kinki rainy-season outlook when published (the JMA's official baiu page states the season typically runs from early June to late July; the tail beyond June 30 is adjacent-Q3 context only and is not part of the 2027 Q2 research coverage).

evidence.observed_facts: The official Japan Meteorological Agency climate page (data.jma.go.jp/cpd/longfcst/en/tourist_baiu.html, fetched 2026-08-13) states the baiu (tsuyu) is a cloudy and rainy period of early summer in Japan that lasts from early June to late July across all areas except Hokkaido, with Kinki (including Kyoto) experiencing this season. June is the primary rainy-season month within the 2027 Q2 research coverage period, and the season is a logistics consideration for transport reliability, road/outdoor conditions, and visitor movement in the Kinki region.
evidence.inference: The June rainy season in Kinki affects outdoor logistics, transport reliability, and tourism patterns; recorded as a major logistics awareness flag for Joe, never as an elimination and never as a scheduling decision.
